transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just can't get past how rough and worn my face and my hands look. It's really starting to bother me. 

Whenever I have to go into town, I feel like every banker or county person I talk to is just staring right at the cracks, the sun spots, and all the sagging skin. My wife tells me I'm making a big deal out of nothing. She says I just look like a man who's worked outdoors his whole life. But I just can't seem to let it go, and it's getting hard to deal with.

Do you believe that these skin concerns are actually a serious medical disfigurement that others are intentionally mocking or analyzing, or do you feel that your distress is disproportionate to how your skin actually looks?

Well, I... I don't think it's a medical condition or anything like that. I know it's just from years working out in the sun and the dirt. And I don't really think people are intentionally mocking me or laughing behind my back. 

But... it just feels like it's all they can see when they look at me. I guess, deep down, I know my wife is probably right and I'm letting it get to me more than I should. It's just... even knowing that I'm probably blowing it out of proportion, I still can't seem to shake how bad it looks to me.
Do you find yourself spending a significant amount of time each day checking your skin in the mirror, comparing it to others, or trying to fix or cover up these areas?

Yeah, I do. It's... well, especially before I have to leave the property for something important, like a loan meeting at the bank or setting up a table at a craft fair. I'll check the bathroom mirror inside, and then I'll get out to the truck and keep checking the rearview mirror. I just keep turning my hat this way and that, trying to see if I can get the brim to cast a shadow and cover up my face a bit better. 

And I definitely compare. I'll look at my hands and just keep comparing them to the younger workers we have around. I end up doing all this checking and comparing until I realize I've wasted a whole lot of time that I really should be using to get actual work done on the farm. It's frustrating, but I just can't seem to stop myself from doing it.
Do you find yourself performing any repetitive physical actions on your skin, such as picking, rubbing, or scrubbing at the areas that bother you?

No, I wouldn't say I do any of that. I'm not picking at my face or scrubbing it raw or anything like that. I mostly just... look at it. And try to hide it with my hat, like I said. But I'm not physically messing with the skin itself.
Has this preoccupation with your skin caused you to avoid social situations or cancel plans because you were too worried about how you looked?

Yeah, it has. I've actually missed some important calls with bankers, and I've put off making decisions for the farm because I just couldn't get myself looking acceptable enough to sit down with people. And my wife has been wanting to take some photos of me working to help promote our farm retreat and the craft sales, but I've completely stopped agreeing to let her take them. I just can't stand the thought of people seeing those pictures.
